 Order

This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. by accused Nos.2 and 3 to enlarge them on bail in Crime No.14/2023 of Anugondanahalli Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned HCGP and perused the material on record.
3.
The complaint is lodged by one Rajappa, father of the deceased-Pallavi M.R.

The prosecution case is that, marriage of the deceased was performed with accused No.1-Veerendra S.M. on 24 and 25.05.2022 at Sri.Shubhameru Kalyana Mantapa, Chikka Thirupathi, Malur Taluk, Kolar District.
At the time of marriage cash of Rs.2,00,000/- was given to the bridegroom and golden ornaments were given to the bride as well as the bride groom.
The deceased was looked after properly only for two months after the marriage by accused No.1 and his parents that is petitioners herein.
Thereafter all the accused started subjecting the deceased to physical and mental cruelty demanding her to bring a sum of Rs.50,000/- and they sent her to her parental home making unlawful demands.
Inspite of paying a sum of Rs.50,000/-, they continued torturing the deceased and unable to tolerate the said torture she committed suicide by consuming poison on 31.01.2023 at about 9.00 am.

4. It is not in dispute that marriage of the deceased was performed with accused No.1 on 24 and 25.05.2022 and she committed suicide by consuming poison on 31.01.2023, which is within seven years of the date of her marriage.

It is also not in dispute that the deceased committed suicide in her matrimonial home and as per the material collected by the prosecution, petitioner No.2 i.e., the mother-in-law of the deceased shifted deceased to one R.K.B.Sanjeevini Hospital with the help of C.Ws.14 and 15, from where she was shifted for higher treatment as per the Doctor's advice to Manipal Hospital in Whitefield.
However she died without responding to the treatment on 02.02.2023 at about 8.25 am.

sentences.text: The allegations are that the deceased was looked after properly only for two months after the marriage and thereafter all the accused started harassing her mentally and physically and coerced her to bring more dowry and inspite of giving a sum of Rs.50,000/-they were giving her physical and mental torture and unable to tolerate the same she committed suicide by consuming poison.
6. The petitioners are the parents of accused No.1.

Omnibus allegations are made against them that they have also subjected the deceased to physical and mental cruelty and coerced her to bring dowry from her parental home etc.
7.

As per the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners, accused Nos.1 and 2 i.e.,
the husband and father-in-law of the deceased were not present in the house and it was the mother-in-law who was present at the time of incident.
From the material collected by the prosecution, it is clear that it was the mother-in-law who shifted the victim to the hospital after seeing the victim struggling for life.

It is stated that with the help of C.Ws.14 and 15, accused No.3 i.e., mother-in- law shifted the deceased to one R.K.B.Sanjeevini Hospital in Anugondanahalli Hobli and then as per the Doctors advice shifted the victim to Manipal Hospital, Whitefield and inspite of giving treatment, victim died on 02.02.2023 at about 8.25 am.

8. It is submitted by the learned High Court Government Pleader that victim was not in a position to give her statement and therefore no dying declaration was recorded.
9.
The immediate cause for the deceased to commit suicide is not forthcoming.
Prosecution has to establish during trial that the deceased was subject to cruelty by these petitioners soon before her death.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet is already filed.

Petitioners are aged persons and they have undertaken to appear before the trial Court and hence by imposing necessary conditions,
relief sought by the petitioners can be granted.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 shall be released in the event of their arrest in Crime No.14/2023 of Anugondanahalli Police Station, subject to the following conditions:
a) Petitioners shall appear before the jurisdictional Court within a period of 10 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the learned Judge.
b) Petitioners shall furnish proof of their residential address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
 c) Petitioners shall make themselves  available for the purpose of further Munibyrappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165544587/
3 investigation if any as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) Petitioners shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till the conclusion of trial.
e) Petitioners shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
 f) Petitioners shall be regular in  attending the Court proceedings unless  exempted for any genuine cause.
